[[File:Lagoa do Capitão com montanha do pico.jpg|thumb|In the Special Protection Area of Zona Central do [[Pico Island|Pico]], [[Azores]]]]
'''''Juniperus brevifolia''''', the '''Azores juniper''', is a species of [[juniper]] native to the [[Azores]] (on [[Corvo Island|Corvo]], [[Faial Island|Faial]], [[Flores Island (Azores)|Flores]], [[Pico Island|Pico]], [[Santa Maria Island (Azores)|Santa Maria]], [[São Jorge Island|São Jorge]], [[São Miguel Island|São Miguel]], and [[Terceira Island|Terceira]]), where it occurs from sea level up to {{Convert|1,500|m|abbr=on}} elevation.<ref name = Elias/> It is closely related to ''[[Juniperus oxycedrus]]'' (prickly juniper) of the [[Mediterranean region]] and ''[[Juniperus cedrus]]'' (Canary Islands juniper) of the neighboring [[Macaronesia]]n islands. It is threatened by [[habitat loss]].<ref name=adams>Adams, R. P. (2004). ''Junipers of the World''. Trafford. {{ISBN|1-4120-4250-X}}</ref><ref name=farjon>Farjon, A. (2005). ''Monograph of Cupressaceae and Sciadopitys''. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. {{ISBN|1-84246-068-4}}</ref><ref name=IUCN>{{cite iucn |author=Thomas, P. |year=2011 |errata=2018 |title=''Juniperus brevifolia'' |volume=2011 |article-number=e.T30326A136559787 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2011-1.RLTS.T30326A9536313.en |access-date=1 November 2023}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to a height of {{Convert|6|m|abbr=on}} and a trunk diameter up to {{Convert|50|cm}}. The [[leaves]] are [[evergreen]], needle-like, in whorls of three, glaucous green, {{Convert|4–10|mm|frac=4}} long and 1–3 mm broad, with a double white [[stoma]]tal band (split by a green midrib) on the inner surface. It is [[dioecious]], with separate male and female plants. The [[conifer cone|seed cones]] are [[Berry (botany)|berry]]-like, green ripening in 18 months to orange-red with a variable pink waxy coating; they are spherical, 6–9 mm diameter, and have three or six fused scales in one or two whorls of three, the three larger scales each with a single [[seed]]. The seeds are dispersed when [[bird]]s eat the cones, digesting the fleshy scales and passing the hard seeds in their droppings. The male cones are yellow, 2–3 mm long, and fall soon after shedding their [[pollen]] in early spring.<ref name=adams/><ref name=farjon/>

==Subdivisions and habitat==
Three subdivisions are accepted.<ref name = powo/> They vary in form and habitat.<ref name = Elias>Elias, Rui Bento, and Eduardo Dias. 2014. "The Recognition of Infraspecific Taxa in ''Juniperus brevifolia'' (Cupressaceae)". ''Phytotaxa'' 188 (5):241–250. https://doi.org/10.11646/phytotaxa.188.5.1.</ref>
*''Juniperus brevifolia'' subsp. ''brevifolia'' – a small to medium tree found between 300 and 1000 metres elevation on Corvo, Faial, Flores, Pico, Santa Maria, Sao Jorge, Sao Miguel, and Terceira.<ref name = Elias/> It grows in a variety of habitats, including ''Juniperus''–''[[Laurus azorica]]'' forest, ''Juniperus''–[[Ilex perado|''Ilex perado'' subsp. ''azorica'']] forest, in pure ''Juniperus'' woods and ''Juniperus''–''[[Sphagnum]]'' woods, and in pioneer scrubland on lava flows with ''[[Erica azorica]]'', ''[[Calluna vulgaris]]'', and ''[[Vaccinium cylindraceum]]''.<ref name=IUCN/>
*''Juniperus brevifolia'' subsp. ''maritima'' {{small|R.B.Elias & E.Días}} – an erect shrub or small tree native to coastal scrubs below 100 metres on Flores, Terceira, Pico and São Jorge,<ref name = Elias/> often growing with ''[[Myrica faya]]'' and ''Erica azorica''.<ref name=IUCN/>
*''Juniperus brevifolia'' var. ''montana'' {{small|R.B.Elias & E.Días}} – a small prostrate shrub common in mountain scrubs and blanket bogs between 850 and 1500 metres elevation,<ref name = Elias/> often with ''Calluna vulgaris''.<ref name=IUCN/>

==Conservation==
This is a [[vulnerable species]] in its native range due to a combination of historical felling for the valuable wood and competition from [[invasive plant|invasive]] introduced plants.<ref name=IUCN/>

On the island of [[Graciosa]], ''Juniperus brevifolia'' has gone extinct, and on the other islands, it remains endangered.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Bettencourt |first1=Sílvia Xavier |last2=Mendonça |first2=Duarte |last3=Lopes |first3=Maria Susana |last4=Rocha |first4=Sara |last5=Monjardino |first5=Paulo |last6=Monteiro |first6=Lisandra |last7=da Câmara Machado |first7=Artur |date=April 2015 |title=Genetic diversity and population structure of the endemic Azorean juniper, ''Juniperus brevifolia'' (Seub.) Antoine, inferred from SSRs and ISSR markers |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0305197815000502 |journal=Biochemical Systematics and Ecology |language=en |volume=59 |pages=314–324 |doi=10.1016/j.bse.2015.02.003|bibcode=2015BioSE..59..314B |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The decline in population is due to [[habitat fragmentation]]s of its preferred habitat ([[laurel forest]]) caused by island colonization and grazing pressures.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fernández-Palacios |first1=José María |last2=de Nascimento |first2=Lea |last3=Otto |first3=Rüdiger |last4=Delgado |first4=Juan D. |last5=García-del-Rey |first5=Eduardo |last6=Arévalo |first6=José Ramón |last7=Whittaker |first7=Robert J. |date=10 December 2010 |title=A reconstruction of Palaeo-Macaronesia, with particular reference to the long-term biogeography of the Atlantic island laurel forests |journal=Journal of Biogeography |volume=38 |issue=2 |pages=226–246 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2699.2010.02427.x |s2cid=86477003 }}</ref>
